verses.text: Agrippa told Paul, “You’ve got the floor. Speak for yourself.” Paul lifted his hand and started his defense.
“King Agrippa, I’m glad I can answer all the Jewish charges in front of you today,
“especially since you know Jewish customs and disputes inside out. Please hear me out—be patient with me.
“All the Jews know how I lived from when I was young, first with my people and then in Jerusalem.
“They’ve known me for ages. If they’ll be honest, I lived as a Pharisee—the strictest crew in our religion.
“Now I’m on trial because I’m holding on to the promise God made our ancestors.
“Our twelve tribes serve God night and day, hoping that promise comes through. King Agrippa, that hope is why the Jews are accusing me!
“Why is it so hard to believe that God raises the dead?
“I used to be convinced I had to go against Jesus of Nazareth in every way.
“That’s exactly what I did in Jerusalem. With the chief priests’ authority, I locked many of God’s people in prison. When they were sentenced to death, I voted for it.
“I punished them again and again in synagogues, trying to force them to blaspheme. I was furious with them and chased them down even in foreign cities.
“That’s why I was on the road to Damascus, carrying the chief priests’ authority and orders.
“Around noon, Your Majesty, I saw a light from heaven on the road—brighter than the sun—shining around me and the people traveling with me.
“We all hit the ground. Then I heard a voice in Hebrew: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? You’re only hurting yourself by kicking against the goads.’
“I asked, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, the one you’re persecuting.’
“‘Get up and stand on your feet. I appeared to you to appoint you as my servant and witness. You’ll tell people what you’ve seen and what I’ll show you later.
“‘I’ll rescue you from your own people and the Gentiles. I’m sending you to them
“‘to open their eyes, so they can turn from darkness to light and from Satan’s power to God. They’ll receive forgiveness of sins and a share among those made holy through faith in me.’
“So, King Agrippa, I didn’t ignore that vision from heaven.
“I preached first in Damascus, then Jerusalem and all Judea, and also to the Gentiles: turn back to God and live like you mean it.
“That’s why the Jews grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
“But God backed me up, so I’m still here today, telling everyone—from the small names to the big ones—only what Moses and the prophets said would happen:
“the Messiah would suffer, rise first from the dead, and announce light to our people and to the Gentiles.”
While Paul was still defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you’ve lost it! All this learning is driving you crazy!”
Paul answered, “I haven’t lost it, Your Excellency Festus. I’m saying true things clearly and with a sound mind.
“The king knows about all this, and I can speak to him straight. I’m sure none of it has escaped him, because it didn’t happen in a back room.
“King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
Agrippa said to Paul, “You think you can talk me into becoming a Christian this fast?”
Paul said, “Fast or slow, I pray to God that you—and everyone listening today—will become like me, chains aside.”
The king stood up, along with the governor, Bernice, and the people sitting with them.
As they left, they said to each other, “This man hasn’t done anything that deserves death or prison.”
Agrippa told Festus, “This man could’ve been set free if he hadn’t appealed to Caesar.”
